cluster_name: Spain and Morocco reinforce Ceuta border after mass migrant crossing
tldr: The most notable divergence at headline level is Russian state media RT, which uniquely labels Ceuta a 'migrant-swarmed enclave' and leads with rape statistics — charged framing absent from all 25 other titles in the corpus. The dominant global headline frame is security enforcement: six outlet groups across China, Turkey, pan-African, US right, Russian Africa, and UK broadsheet all foreground Spain and Morocco's joint crackdown rather than migrant agency or legal status. A strong counter-current, carried by wire services, both Deutsche Welle feeds, and three Asian outlets, foregrounds humanitarian suffering — unaccompanied minors abandoned on the streets and migrant women reporting sexual harassment. Spain's domestic and US right-leaning outlets concentrate the policy-failure angle on Madrid's legal violations and slow response, while Brazilian, French-state, and one Russian outlet are the only ones to surface the asylum-rights legal dimension at headline level. RT Africa is the sole headline in the corpus to surface Morocco's territorial sovereignty claim over Ceuta and Melilla — a geopolitical frame entirely invisible in all other titles.
event_summary: An estimated 70,000–80,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta in late July 2026; weeks later, thousands remain stranded on the beach, Morocco and Spain are reinforcing the border after online calls for a second crossing, and unaccompanied minors and migrant women face severe conditions on the ground.

silences.what_they_covered_instead: BBC Africa ran a framing-neutral explanatory question ('What triggered the mass migrant crossings into Ceuta?') — a question format that assigns no directional frame at headline level rather than asserting security, humanitarian, or policy angles.

single_outlet_findings.finding: RT is the only outlet in the corpus to use the compound 'migrant-swarmed' — inflammatory language absent from all 25 other headlines — while simultaneously leading with rape statistics, placing the story's moral weight on crime rather than displacement, policy, or legal status.

RT Africa's 'Spain rejects Morocco's claim to sovereignty over enclaves' is the sole headline in the corpus to surface the territorial sovereignty dispute: all other outlets treat Ceuta's status as immutable backdrop rather than contested subject.
El Mundo's captured title is 'Política' — a section label, not an article headline — making this outlet's framing unreadable at the headline layer from this dataset.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, the Ceuta crisis splits between a dominant security-enforcement register — Spain and Morocco jointly cracking down — and a humanitarian counter-current of minors abandoned and women harassed, with Russian state media RT uniquely injecting a crime frame via the charged compound 'migrant-swarmed' and rape statistics absent from every other title. Spain's conservative press concentrates the policy-failure angle on Madrid's legal violations, while the territorial sovereignty dispute and public-health dimensions visible in body text are almost entirely suppressed across the broader headline landscape.
